confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion and all 9 PDF pages, including references and the final license page; no appendix or supplementary material is identified. The source.version description is accurate: ICIDIT 2023 proceedings, Atlantis Highlights in Intelligent Systems 10, copyright 2024, printed pp. 451-459 (PDF pp. 1-9).
The title and sole author Yiyi Zhao match source.title_on_document and source.authors_on_document (PDF p. 1, title block).

ai_vs_human is supported for both design_class and context_class: section 3.2 compares AIGC-generated design with artificial/manual design. Random sampling describes questionnaire recruitment; no random assignment of people to generative-AI assistance or randomized condition order is documented (PDF p. 5, sections 3.1-3.2; full-document review).

The stated questionnaire sample is 50 design professionals, with Sample Size 50 repeated in all six Table 1 rows. The form appropriately identifies this as a respondent count and leaves randomized counts and creator-arm counts null; distinct respondents by method, exclusions and the number of logo creators are not stated (PDF p. 5, section 3.1 items (3)-(4), Table 1).

The innovation reported string and one_line_finding match Table 1: AIGC mean 7.110, SD 0.437; manual design mean 8.550, SD 0.253; Sample Size 50 in each row. The innovation scale runs from 1 (Very unoriginal) to 10 (very innovative), and no inferential test accompanies the comparison (PDF p. 5, section 3.2 and Table 1; PDF p. 6, Innovation score).

The aesthetics reported string matches Table 1: AIGC mean 8.770, SD 0.252; manual design mean 7.600, SD 0.303; Sample Size 50 in each row. The scale runs from 1 (very unaesthetic) to 10 (very aesthetic), with no inferential test reported (PDF p. 5, section 3.2 and Table 1; PDF p. 6, Aesthetic score).

The brand-expression reported string correctly preserves the source discrepancy: Table 1 gives AIGC mean 6.950, SD 0.171 and manual design mean 8.750, SD 0.152, with Sample Size 50 per row; the prose instead gives manual-design SD 0.253. The scale runs from 1 (very inaccurate) to 10 (very accurate), with no inferential test reported (PDF p. 5, section 3.2 and Table 1; PDF p. 6, Brand Expression Score).

Stable-Diffusion, Dream Studio.ai and Prodia are illustrated using a clothing-brand brief with red, gold and Chinese elements, but the empirical comparison does not specify which tool or version generated the rated logos (PDF pp. 2-5, section 2.3, Figures 1-3 and section 3.2).

The paper is not a synthesis and reports no pooled estimates. Its additional feedback and sentiment analysis do not establish randomized AI assistance or a scored measure of diversity across creators; leaving synthesis fields at their defaults and coding the three logo-rating outcomes as question none is supported (PDF pp. 5-7, sections 3.1-3.2 and Conclusions).
summary: The paper reports an AI-versus-human logo-rating comparison with 50 questionnaire respondents, but no documented random assignment of people to AI assistance. All reported numbers and source-version details match the PDF; correct the unsupported creative-participant sample-size eligibility flag and complete the three contrast records.
